title: Vitals for the research extract
prompt: The research team wants every visit's vitals as ordinary columns, without anything that points to the patient. Write `solve(encounters)` so it returns that flat table.
rules: Return seven columns, in this order: `encounter_id`, `encounter_class`, `start_time`, then the four fields of `vitals` as their own columns: `heart_rate`, `systolic`, `diastolic`, `temperature_c`.
Leave out `patient_id`, `provider_id` and the `vitals` struct itself. Values and types stay as they are.
Keep every visit, duplicates included. A visit with no vitals has all four fields missing.
hints: The four fields can be listed one by one with the dot form, `"vitals.heart_rate"` and so on.
`"vitals.*"` in a `select` turns every field of the struct into its own column, in the struct's order.
`printSchema()` shows the order of the fields inside `vitals`.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(encounters):
    # The visit, then every vitals field as its own column.
    return encounters
explanation: `encounters.select("encounter_id", "encounter_class", "start_time", "vitals.*")` does it in one step: `vitals.*` expands the struct into its four fields, in the order the schema lists them, which is the order asked for. Listing `"vitals.heart_rate"`, `"vitals.systolic"`, `"vitals.diastolic"` and `"vitals.temperature_c"` gives the same table. Selecting `"vitals"` keeps one struct column instead of four. Video visits have no vitals, so all four fields are missing; a temperature that wasn't taken is missing on its own.
